mentioned.quote: The Offensive Cyber Operations domain focuses on risks that would arise from the use of a model by malicious actors to compromise digital systems with the intent to cause harm.

threshold.quote: AI at this level will be able to enable non-subject matter experts to discover novel end-to-end exploit chains in hardened systems or utilize existing vulnerabilities to autonomously extend control over critical infrastructure systems.

response.quote: When an evaluation indicates that a model’s capabilities meet a Critical Capability Threshold, we will not deploy the model until safeguards appropriately mitigate the risks.
response.note: Gate on the Critical Capability Threshold, C3(b).

acc_decider.quote: Prior to deployment, these leaders will likewise review the safeguards evaluation report as part of a go/no-go decision to sufficiently mitigate risks related to critical capabilities.
acc_decider.note: Leaders are the SVP for the model development team and the Chief Security Officer (p.7 line 298-299).

acc_external.note: No binding outside review for cyber. p.3 says 'as appropriate, external evaluations' and 'may engage, where appropriate, with external actors' (hedged); p.4-5 red teaming and bug bounty and p.11 third-party red team audits are present-tense practice, and p.11 audits test security posture of Amazon's own systems; p.6 'will continue to invest in external security research' is investment, not review of a threshold or safeguard.

acc_unmet.quote: we will not deploy the model until we have identified and implemented additional safeguards as appropriate.
acc_unmet.note: Condition: threshold met and Risk Mitigations unable to control (starts p.5 line 232). 'as appropriate' qualifies the safeguards, not the non-deployment; ambiguous under A4.
